notes.decision: Standard Manichaean five-fold dark cosmology: five storehouses, five archons, five spirits, five bodies, five tastes — each register corresponding to the five worlds (smoke, fire, wind, water, darkness).
Read as ⲧⲡⲉ 'taste' — gustatory correspondence-register completing the five-fold schema. Each dark world has its taste-correspondence as its bodily register.
Greek loanword στοιχεῖον 'element.' The orthography ⲥⲧⲟⲭⲉⲓϣⲛ at start of line 20 may be a scribal slip for ⲥⲧⲟⲭⲉⲓⲱⲛ; preserved as transcribed.
Lexeme unclear. Translated 'wellspring' interpretively, fitting the context of 'origin/source of all evil and wickedness.' Possibly related to a root meaning 'pit, abyss, source.'
ⲥⲱⲣ = 'scatter, spread.' The ⲧⲃⲛ- prefix unclear, possibly intensifier or article + nominalizer. Translated 'scattering-forth' to capture the noun of action.
Abstract noun from ⲧⲱⲛ 'rise up against, contend' — 'contention, strife.' Doubled ⲧⲧ may be writing convention.
πύλη + ⲥⲱⲭⲉ. ⲥⲱⲭⲉ tentatively rendered 'slaughter/wounding' — fits the martial inventory (battles, dangers, gates of X). Possibly related to a root meaning 'strike, smite.'
ⲭⲁⲥⲉ = 'high, lofty' (Lycopolitan reflex of ⲭⲱⲥⲉ/ϫⲓⲥⲉ — cf. accumulated vocab ⲡⲭⲥⲉ). 'The lofty kingship' = the elevated dominion of the King of Darkness over the dark realms.

ⲉⲕ[...] is the personal name of the King of Darkness, restored by editor as 'ⲉⲕⲓⲁ' (or similar). Possibly Greek αἰκία 'outrage, mistreatment' as personified epithet, or a transliterated demonic name. Reading uncertain.

ⲟⲩⲛ ... ⲛϩⲏⲧϩ = 'there are ... in him.' The King of Darkness has five animal-forms as the five-fold composition of his body — head of lion, hands/feet of demons, shoulders of eagle, belly of dragon, tail of fish (continuing onto next page).
Reading uncertain. The damaged sequence after 'demons and...' may include a second class of evil beings paired with demons (e.g. devils, evil ones), but the abbreviation/orthography ⲓ̈ϩ is unclear.

Translated 'her tail' taking ⲥⲉⲧ as Lyc. variant of Sah. ⲥⲁⲧ 'tail,' with 3sg fem possessive ⲡⲉϩ- (= Sah. ⲡⲉⲥ-). The fish-tail comparison and morphology context support this. ⲧⲁⲃⲉϩ is left untranslated — the term resists clear identification (possibly a flat fish, leech, or specific body-part).

Translated 'five other vehicles' — ⲟⲭⲏⲙⲁ (Greek ὄχημα) is the standard Manichaean term for cosmic vehicles/chariots. The list of five (darkness, mire, [ⲃⲁⲉ], bitterness, burning) corresponds to the Manichaean schema of five worlds/elements of darkness, though not in the canonical order.
Translated 'measure of irons.' ⲡⲉ̄ⲓϣ probably = Lyc. ⲡⲱϣ 'measure, portion'; ⲃⲁⲛⲓⲡⲉ = 'irons' (pl.). The context is iron heated red-hot from fire as image of the burning element.
Translated 'of receiving-matter' — verbal compound ⲭⲓ ('receive') + ⲍⲩⲗⲏ ('matter'). The matter that receives forms is identified as the Enthymesis of Death — standard Manichaean cosmology.
Greek loanword ζωγραφεῖν 'to paint, depict.' Matter 'painted herself through the nature of the dark land' — i.e. she fashioned her own image using dark substance.

Translated 'the bronze and the lead' — ⲍⲁⲙⲧ̄ = Sah. ϩⲟⲙⲧ̄ 'bronze'; ⲡⲁⲉⲓⲛⲉ likely a Lyc. variant for a metal in the iron/bronze/lead/tin sequence. The point is that no metal is harder than the archonic body of matter.
ⲕⲟⲡⲓⲥ = Greek κοπίς 'cleaver, knife'; ⲁⲡⲧⲏⲣϥ̄ 'at all/in the All' as adverbial intensifier. Translated 'no knife at all' — the archon's body is unsplittable by any iron tool.

Tentatively rendered 'concealment.' Coptic ϩⲱⲧⲡ ('set, conceal') and ϩⲱⲧⲃ ('slay') both fit the Lyc. spelling ⲍⲱⲧⲃⲉ. Context favours 'concealment in speech of her members,' since Matter conceals her son and reveals him alternately (segments 19–21).
ⲍⲟⲙⲓⲗⲓⲁ = Greek ὁμιλία 'company, conversation.' ⲥⲉⲃⲉ taken as Lyc. for ⲥⲱⲃⲉ 'mockery, folly'; alternative reading 'wisdom' (Sah. ⲥⲁⲃⲉ) does not fit the negative cosmic register here.
Translated 'magics.' ⲍⲓⲕ = Lyc. ϩⲓⲕ 'magic, sorcery.' The contemporary magical arts are framed as mysteries belonging to the kingdom of darkness.
Idiom ϩⲱⲛ ⲉⲧⲟⲟⲧ⸗ 'command' (literally 'lay charge upon the hand of'). Translated 'I command you.' Speaker is the Apostle to his elect.
Translated 'receive teaching.' ⲥⲃⲱ rendered consistently as 'teaching' per terminology guideline.

Translated 'verdict ... cut off.' ⲁⲡⲟⲫⲁⲥⲓⲥ = formal sentence (Greek ἀπόφασις, per accumulated vocabulary); ϣⲱⲧⲥ̄ '(they) cut her off' uses the same root as ϣⲱⲱⲧ 'decree/cut' — preserving the dual force of legal pronouncement and severance.

Translated as 'thirty-third.' The form ⲧⲙⲁⲍ-ⲱⲁⲙⲧ̄ literally parses as ⲧⲙⲉϩ-ϣⲟⲙⲛⲧ̄ ('the third'), but the leading ⲧⲧ-, plus the chapter's position in the codex (page 32, after the two-trees kephalaion), makes this almost certainly a compressed compound numeral — likely 'thirty-third' (ⲧⲙⲉϩ-ⲙⲁⲁⲃ-ϣⲟⲙⲛⲧ̄ contracted via haplography to ⲧⲙⲁⲍ-ⲱⲁⲙⲧ̄). Identified as Polotsky/Böhlig K.33 'On the Gate of Darkness.' Confidence moderate.

Translated 'the scent of the five worlds.' ⲧⲉⲥⲧⲉ from ⲥⲧⲟⲓ 'smell, scent.' The numeral ⲡⲉϩⲧⲟⲩ formally matches ⲡϩⲧⲁⲩ 'the four' from prior vocabulary; however, the Manichaean cosmological context (Five Worlds of Darkness ruled by the Prince of Darkness — smoke, fire, wind, water, darkness) overwhelmingly favors 'five.' The form may represent a Lyc orthographic variant for ⲡϯⲟⲩ 'the five' rather than a true ⲡϩⲧⲁⲩ.
Translated 'perceiving.' ⲣ̄-ⲛⲟⲓ 'do/exercise perception, understand' (cf. ⲛⲟⲉⲓ Greek νοεῖν). The circumstantial ϩ-/ⲉϥ- frames the gate's mode of knowing.
Translated 'sealed up in their mouths.' ⲥⲁⲧⲙⲉϩ taken as qualitative of ⲥⲱⲧⲙ̄ 'shut, close,' with ⲉϩⲁ- forming a perfect circumstantial. The gate perceives even what is unspoken/sealed within speech.
Translated 'signaling.' ⲭⲱⲣⲙⲉ = ϫⲱⲣⲙ 'wink, signal'; ⲧ-ⲟⲓⲛ-ⲭⲱⲣⲙⲉ likely 'the act of signaling/winking.' Continues the theme of secret communication that the gate nonetheless perceives.

Translated 'sense-perception.' ⲁⲓ̈ⲥⲑⲁⲛⲉ = Greek αἰσθάνομαι/αἴσθησις. The gate's epistemic limit: it operates only by sensible perception of what is before its eyes, not by intellective grasp of inner faculties (mind, thought, reflection).
Translated 'hidden.' Tentatively read as a qualitative form related to ⲱⲡ/ⲍⲏⲡ 'hidden, concealed' — the 'other hidden matter' is the chapter's second topic.

Translated 'great sphere of iron.' ⲃⲁⲛⲓⲡⲉ = ⲃⲉⲛⲓⲡⲉ 'iron' — the cosmological-correspondential image: the gate of darkness manifests AS a great iron sphere falling like a cloud. Iron in Manichaean correspondence = the body/realm of darkness.
Translated 'joined together.' Read as qualitative of ϩⲱⲧⲣ̄ 'be joined, yoked' with reciprocal -ⲉⲣⲏⲩ → ⲓⲱⲩ. The limbs draw together to form one iron sphere.
Translated 'is likened to the thunder.' ⲧⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲛⲧ qualitative of ⲧⲱⲛⲧⲛ̄ 'be like'; ⲡⲍⲣⲟⲩⲙⲡⲉ = ⲡϩⲣⲟⲩⲙⲡⲉ 'thunder.' Continues the cloud-sphere-thunder theophanic complex.
Translated 'birds' / 'the bird.' Lyc ϩⲁⲗⲏⲧ 'bird, fowl.' The simile compares scattered (powers? archons?) to dispersed birds.

Untranslated (left in placeholder). Possibly ⲁⲛⲁⲅⲕⲏ 'necessity, constraint' (Greek loan) or related to ⲱϫⲛ 'failure'; alternatively a corrupt form of ⲁⲣⲭⲱⲛ 'archon.' Context: 'these evil signs exist in the X of the demons.'
Translated 'casts out.' Likely Lyc ⲧⲛⲛⲟⲟⲩ/ⲛⲟⲩⲕⲉ 'throw, cast.' The dark land disgorges/casts forth its denizens.
Translated 'in the fury.' ⲃⲗ̄ⲕⲉ = ⲃⲱⲗⲕ 'fury, rage' (Crum 39a). Standard Coptic noun for divine/demonic anger.

Translated 'the under-archons' reading ϩⲩⲃ-/ϩⲩⲡ- as Greek ὑπ- prefix indicating subordinate rulers. The form ⲩⲃ̂ may reflect scribal variation; the comparative ⲛ̄ⲍⲟⲩⲟ ('more than') frames a hierarchy of archons.
Translated 'the powers' per accumulated vocabulary, which identifies ⲛⲟⲁⲙ as a Lycopolitan variant of ϫⲟⲙ 'power, might.' The overdots may mark a special technical term in the manuscript.

Read as ⲧⲓⲡⲉ (= Sahidic ϯⲡⲉ) 'the taste.' This is decisively confirmed by line 28: ⲧ⳧ⲡⲉ ⲉⲧⲍⲁⲗⲟ̄ ⲉⲧⲍⲛ̄ ⳧ⲡⲉ ⲛⲓⲙ 'the sweet taste that is in every taste.' The ⳧ glyph appears to represent a special ligature or abbreviation but functionally encodes the same word throughout.

Translated 'the projection' for this recurring fourth cosmological property (after body, taste, fruit). The term names the king's downward extension into earthly realms — the metal IS the king's reach into worldly principalities. Etymology unclear; possibly from ⲉⲓⲧⲛ̄ 'lower part' with abstract suffix, or related to ϯ 'give' as 'that-which-is-given/projected.' Translation tentative; see proposed terms.
Translated 'raging' tentatively, deriving from ϫⲣⲟ 'be strong, prevail, rage.' Context (archons humbling humanity in tyranny) supports a verb of violent activity.
Read as Lycopolitan reflex of ⲍⲓϫⲛ 'upon, over' rather than ⲁϫⲛ 'without.' Context requires 'reigning over creation,' not 'reigning without creation.'
Translated 'foremost' from ⲥⲟⲩⲓⲧ/ϣⲟⲣⲡ̄ 'first.' Standard cosmological epithet — the lion is the chief/foremost of beasts, mapping to the fire-king's primacy.
Greek θηρίον plural 'wild beasts.' The lambda for rho is a known Lycopolitan/Manichaean orthographic variation.

Translated 'eagle' from ⲁϩⲱⲙ 'eagle' (Crum 25b). The eagle-face of the wind-king is consistent with Manichaean cosmological lore (cf. parallel beast-faces: lion=fire, eagle=wind, fish=water, dragon=darkness).
Translated 'sharp' from ⲕⲱϩ 'sharpen' qualitative ⲕⲏϩ 'sharp' (with Lycopolitan ⲭ for ⲕ). The taste of wind being sharp/piercing fits the elemental correspondence.
Parsed as ⲡⲁ- (relational) + ⲙⲛⲧ-ⲱⲙⲱⲉⲉ ('worship,' = ϣⲙϣⲉ) + ⲉⲓⲁⲱⲗⲟⲛ (εἴδωλον 'idol') = 'the one of idol-worship.' Wind manifests as pagan idolatry.

Tentatively translated 'altars.' The form is unclear — possibly a Lycopolitan term related to ⲟⲉⲓⲱⲙⲉ or analogous shrine-vocabulary. Context (paired with images, idol-places, worship-places) supports a cultic-architectural sense.
Translated 'the established images.' ⲛⲕⲱ taken as qualitative of ⲕⲱ 'set, place' — 'the set/established (images).'
Translated 'a fish-face' (ⲍⲁ = 'face/aspect' + ⲛⲧⲃⲧ 'of fish'). The water-king's face matches the elemental (fish), parallel with lion-faced fire-king and eagle-faced wind-king.

Translated 'the dark-stone' tentatively. Possibly Greek βάσανος 'touchstone' (a black stone used to test gold) or a metallurgical term for a dark mineral/dross paired with lead in the darkness-realm. The doubled metal (lead + dark-stone) for the world of Darkness mirrors the doubled metals (gold + lead) of the smoke-world.

Translated 'the bitter [one]' from ⲥⲏϣⲉ/ⲥⲓϣⲉ 'be bitter, gall.' The gustatory register is established by the immediately preceding ⲧϯⲡⲉ 'the taste,' fitting the Manichaean correspondential schema where the realm of the five spirits of darkness has a bitter taste (cf. ⲡϣⲏⲛ ⲉⲧⲍⲁⲩ 'the bitter tree'). Alternative ⲥⲁϣⲉ 'stripe, blow' would yield 'the lash' but does not fit the gustatory parallelism.

Read as Lycopolitan reduction of Greek ⲃⲁⲥⲁⲛⲟⲥ (βάσανος) 'torment, trial, ordeal.' Translated 'the torment.' The pairing with 'taste' and 'fruit' suggests this is the gustatory-experiential register of the dark spirits' work.

Translated 'the foretellers,' parsing as ⲛⲉⲧ-ϣⲁ(ⲣⲡ̄)-ⲣⲧ or related to ϣⲣ̄ⲡ 'first, before' = those who do something in advance, hence prognosticators. Parallel to ⲣⲉϥϯⲙⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'sign-givers' and 'spirits which inquire,' all in a divinatory list. Alternative readings considered: 'those who tremble' (ecstatics), 'those who scatter (lots)' — none confirmed.

Treated end-of-line ⲭⲉ as ϫⲉ introducing direct discourse ('saying:') after ϯⲭⲱ ⲙⲙⲁⲥ ⲁⲣⲱⲧⲛ̄ 'I say it to you.' Line 8 then begins the imperative ⲱⲗ 'lift up, take up' (= ⲱⲗⲉ/ⲱⲗⲓ), governing ⲡⲉⲧⲛⲍⲏⲧ 'your heart' — a hortatory call to interior attention parallel to 'cast away from yourselves' that follows.

Translated 'cast away.' The verb (with ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth') functions as the soteriological complement to 'lift up your heart' — interior attention paired with renunciation. Etymology uncertain; possibly related to ⲧⲟⲩⲱⲑⲛⲉ 'discharge, expel.'

Translated 'practice' tentatively. The form is an abstract (ⲙⲛⲧ-) noun whose root ⲟⲁⲟⲩⲁⲛ is unidentified. Context places it parallel to 'garment of worship' and 'conducting-of-life (politeia)' — three terms for embodied participation in the dark spirits' realm. 'Practice/comportment' captures the parallel sense pending lexical parallels.
Translated 'their judgment.' Likely from ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon, judge' with nominal form ⲙⲡⲉ; paired here with ⲕⲟⲗⲁⲥⲓⲥ 'punishment.' Standard eschatological collocation 'judgment and punishment.'
